---
title: "One-month Treasury yield cash illustration"
output: html_document
date: "2026-10-16"
---

The CSV contains monthly dated values for [FRED DGS1MO](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS1MO), an annualized one-month Treasury constant-maturity yield quoted in percent. FRED publishes the series daily; the CSV does not record how its monthly values were selected or aggregated. This illustration applies each CSV yield for one month at `yield / 1200` and reinvests the result. It is an approximation, not a measured Treasury bill total-return series. It excludes trading costs, taxes, and timing differences between the quote date and investment date.

## Cash illustration

```{r cash-illustration, echo=TRUE}
data <- read.csv("Monthly TBill Data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(names(data), c("observation_date", "DGS1MO")))

dates <- as.Date(data$observation_date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
yield_pct <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data$DGS1MO))
stopifnot(nrow(data) >= 2L,
          !anyNA(dates), !anyNA(yield_pct),
          all(is.finite(yield_pct)),
          all(yield_pct / 1200 > -1))

ordered <- order(dates)
dates <- dates[ordered]
yield_pct <- yield_pct[ordered]
month_id <- as.integer(format(dates, "%Y")) * 12L +
            as.integer(format(dates, "%m"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(month_id),
          all(diff(month_id) == 1L),
          all(format(dates, "%d") == "01"))

monthly_approx_return <- yield_pct / 1200
wealth <- cumprod(1 + monthly_approx_return)
running_peak <- cummax(c(1, wealth))[-1]
drawdown <- wealth / running_peak - 1

n <- length(monthly_approx_return)

statistics <- data.frame(
  first_observation = format(dates[1], "%m/%d/%Y"),
  last_observation = format(dates[n], "%m/%d/%Y"),
  observations = n,
  cumulative_approx_return = tail(wealth, 1) - 1,
  ending_value_from_1000 = 1000 * tail(wealth, 1),
  annualized_approx_growth = tail(wealth, 1)^(12 / n) - 1,
  annualized_approx_volatility = sd(monthly_approx_return) * sqrt(12),
  maximum_approx_drawdown = min(drawdown))

print(statistics)
```
